hints: Look past the cell names and ask one question: which of these cells must divide by mitosis over and over again without ageing?
Remember the rule: every mitosis shortens telomeres, so any cell line that must stay dividing for life or for massive clonal expansion needs telomerase to rebuild them.
walkthrough:
**Recall what telomerase is for**

Think of telomeres as protective caps on chromosomes. A little bit is lost at every mitosis.

Most body cells do not make telomerase, so they can only divide a limited number of times before they stop.

**Ask who cannot afford to stop dividing**

Any cell that must keep dividing indefinitely, or divide very rapidly many times in a row, needs to switch the telomerase gene on by transcription.

That keeps telomeres long and prevents senescence.

**Apply this to 1, 2 and 3**

1 cancer cells divide uncontrollably and are effectively immortal, so they need telomerase. 2 stem cells must supply new cells for a lifetime, so they need telomerase. 3 activated memory B-lymphocytes must undergo rapid clonal expansion to make many plasma cells quickly, so they also need telomerase.

All three need it, so the answer is 1, 2 and 3.

options.A: Correct. Cancer cells, stem cells and activated memory B-lymphocytes all require many mitotic cycles, so all need to transcribe telomerase.
options.B: Misses out 3. Activated memory B-lymphocytes also divide rapidly by mitosis during clonal expansion and need telomerase.
options.C: Misses out 2. Stem cells must keep dividing throughout life to replace cells, so they definitely need telomerase.
options.D: Misses out 1. Cancer cells reactivate telomerase to become immortal and avoid telomere loss.
